children.note:
ACTIVE ↔ PASSIVE VOICE
│
├── PRESENT
│   │
│   ├── Simple
│   │   Active   → Sub + V1(s/es) + Obj
│   │              👉 She writes a letter
│   │   Passive  → Obj + is/am/are + V3 + by + Sub
│   │              👉 A letter is written by her
│   │
│   ├── Continuous
│   │   Active   → Sub + is/am/are + V1+ing + Obj
│   │              👉 He is playing cricket
│   │   Passive  → Obj + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Sub
│   │              👉 Cricket is being played by him
│   │
│   ├── Perfect
│   │   Active   → Sub + has/have + V3 + Obj
│   │              👉 They have completed the work
│   │   Passive  → Obj + has/have + been + V3 + by + Sub
│   │              👉 The work has been completed by them
│   │
│   └── Perfect Continuous ❌
│       👉 She has been studying for 2 hours
│       👉 (No Passive possible)
│
├── PAST
│   │
│   ├── Simple
│   │   Active   → Sub + V2 + Obj
│   │              👉 He wrote a letter
│   │   Passive  → Obj + was/were + V3 + by + Sub
│   │              👉 A letter was written by him
│   │
│   ├── Continuous
│   │   Active   → Sub + was/were + V1+ing + Obj
│   │              👉 She was reading a book
│   │   Passive  → Obj + was/were + being + V3 + by + Sub
│   │              👉 A book was being read by her
│   │
│   ├── Perfect
│   │   Active   → Sub + had + V3 + Obj
│   │              👉 They had finished the task
│   │   Passive  → Obj + had + been + V3 + by + Sub
│   │              👉 The task had been finished by them
│   │
│   └── Perfect Continuous ❌
│       👉 He had been working for 2 hours
│       👉 (No Passive possible)
│
├── FUTURE
│   │
│   ├── Simple
│   │   Active   → Sub + will/shall + V1 + Obj
│   │              👉 They will visit the museum
│   │   Passive  → Obj + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Sub
│   │              👉 The museum will be visited by them
│   │
│   ├── Continuous ❌
│   │   👉 She will be cooking dinner
│   │   👉 (No Passive possible)
│   │
│   ├── Perfect
│   │   Active   → Sub + will/shall + have + V3 + Obj
│   │              👉 He will have completed the work
│   │   Passive  → Obj + will/shall + have + been + V3 + by + Sub
│   │              👉 The work will have been completed by him
│   │
│   └── Perfect Continuous ❌
│       👉 They will have been traveling
│       👉 (No Passive possible)
│
└── RULE
    ├── Object → Subject
    ├── Use V3 (Past Participle)
    ├── Add helping verb (is/am/are/was/were/been)
    └── by + subject (optional sometimes)

NARRATION (DIRECT → INDIRECT)
│
├── 1. STRUCTURE
│   ├── Reporting Verb → He said
│   ├── Quoted Speech → "I am fine"
│   └── Indirect → He said that he was fine
│
├── 2. TENSE CHANGE (Only if Reporting Verb is Past)
│   │
│   ├── Present → Past
│   │   👉 "I am happy" → was happy
│   │
│   ├── Present Continuous → Past Continuous
│   │   👉 "I am playing" → was playing
│   │
│   ├── Present Perfect → Past Perfect
│   │   👉 "I have done" → had done
│   │
│   ├── Simple Past → Past Perfect
│   │   👉 "I went" → had gone
│   │
│   ├── Past Perfect → No Change
│   │   👉 "I had finished" → had finished
│   │
│   └── Future (will) → would
│       👉 "I will go" → would go
│
├── 3. PRONOUN CHANGE
│   │
│   ├── I → He/She
│   ├── You → I/He/She/They
│   ├── We → They
│   ├── My → His/Her
│   └── Our → Their
│
│   👉 "I love my dog"
│   → He said that he loved his dog
│
├── 4. TIME / PLACE CHANGE
│   │
│   ├── Today → That day
│   ├── Tomorrow → The next day
│   ├── Yesterday → The previous day
│   ├── Now → Then
│   ├── Here → There
│   └── This → That
│
│   👉 "I will go tomorrow"
│   → He said that he would go the next day
│
├── 5. SENTENCE TYPES (MOST IMPORTANT)
│   │
│   ├── (A) ASSERTIVE (STATEMENTS)
│   │   ├── said → said that
│   │   └── Example:
│   │       "I am happy"
│   │       → He said that he was happy
│   │
│   ├── (B) NEGATIVE STATEMENTS
│   │   ├── Keep "not"
│   │   └── Example:
│   │       "I do not like tea"
│   │       → She said that she did not like tea
│   │
│   ├── (C) INTERROGATIVE (QUESTIONS)
│   │   │
│   │   ├── YES/NO
│   │   │   ├── Use if / whether
│   │   │   └── Remove question format
│   │   │
│   │   │   👉 "Do you play?"
│   │   │   → He asked if I played
│   │   │
│   │   ├── WH- QUESTIONS
│   │   │   ├── Keep WH word
│   │   │   └── Statement form
│   │   │
│   │   │   👉 "Where are you going?"
│   │   │   → He asked where I was going
│   │
│   ├── (D) IMPERATIVE (ORDER / REQUEST / ADVICE)
│   │   │
│   │   ├── said to → told / requested / advised / ordered
│   │   ├── Use → to + V1
│   │   └── Negative → not to + V1
│   │
│   │   ├── Examples:
│   │   │   "Sit down"
│   │   │   → He told me to sit down
│   │   │
│   │   │   "Please help me"
│   │   │   → She requested me to help her
│   │   │
│   │   │   "Take rest"
│   │   │   → Doctor advised me to take rest
│   │
│   │   ├── NEGATIVE IMPERATIVE 🔥
│   │   │   "Don't + V1" → not to + V1
│   │   │
│   │   │   👉 "Don't wear this watch"
│   │   │   → He told me not to wear that watch
│   │   │
│   │   │   ❌ to not wear
│   │   │   ❌ that not to
│   │   │   ✔ not to wear
│   │
│   ├── (E) EXCLAMATORY (EMOTION)
│   │   │
│   │   ├── Remove "!"
│   │   ├── Use → exclaimed with joy/sorrow/surprise
│   │   └── Use "that"
│   │
│   │   ├── Examples:
│   │   │   "What a beautiful place!"
│   │   │   → He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful place
│   │   │
│   │   │   "Hurrah! We won"
│   │   │   → She exclaimed with joy that they had won
│   │
│   ├── (F) OPTATIVE (WISH / PRAYER)
│   │   │
│   │   ├── Use → wished / prayed
│   │   └── Use "that"
│   │
│   │   ├── Examples:
│   │   │   "May you succeed"
│   │   │   → He wished that I might succeed
│   │   │
│   │   │   "God bless you"
│   │   │   → She prayed that God might bless me
│
├── 6. PRONOUN CASE
│   │
│   ├── 1st → I, We → me, us
│   ├── 2nd → You → you
│   └── 3rd → He/She/They → him/her/them
│
└── 7. COMMON RULES
    ├── Remove quotes (" ")
    ├── Use connectors → that / if / WH
    ├── Change pronoun
    ├── Change tense (if needed)
    └── Change time/place words

Exact words are written inside quotation marks.
Example: He said, "I am happy."

The same idea is reported without quotation marks.
Example: He said that he was happy.

GERUND vs INFINITIVE vs CAUSATIVE
│
├── GERUND (V + ing)
│
│   ├── Use
│   │   ├── Habit / Experience
│   │   ├── Enjoyment
│   │   ├── Real or completed action
│   │   └── After prepositions
│   │
│   ├── Structure
│   │   └── Verb + ing
│   │
│   ├── Important Rule
│   │   └── After preposition → always V+ing
│   │
│   ├── Common Verbs
│   │   ├── enjoy
│   │   ├── avoid
│   │   ├── finish
│   │   ├── suggest
│   │   └── keep
│   │
│   ├── Examples
│   │   ├── She is fond of reading.
│   │   ├── He is good at playing football.
│   │   └── I enjoy playing cricket.
│
├── INFINITIVE (to + V1)
│
│   ├── Use
│   │   ├── Purpose
│   │   ├── Intention / Decision
│   │   ├── Future action
│   │   └── After adjectives
│   │
│   ├── Structure
│   │   └── to + V1
│   │
│   ├── Common Verbs
│   │   ├── want
│   │   ├── decide
│   │   ├── plan
│   │   ├── hope
│   │   └── promise
│   │
│   ├── Examples
│   │   ├── I am happy to see you.
│   │   ├── He went to market to buy fruits.
│   │   └── I want to go home.
│
├── CAUSATIVE VERBS
│
│   ├── Meaning
│   │   └── Make or cause someone to do something
│   │
│   ├── Bare Infinitive (Without "to")
│   │   ├── Verbs → make, let
│   │   ├── help → V1 / to + V1
│   │   ├── Structure → Subject + Verb + Object + V1
│   │   └── Examples
│   │       ├── He made me do it.
│   │       ├── She let me go.
│   │       └── She helped me (to) complete the work.
│   │
│   └── To-Infinitive
│       ├── Verbs → tell, ask, allow, force, advise
│       ├── Structure → Subject + Verb + Object + to + V1
│       └── Examples
│           ├── He told me to go.
│           └── The teacher allowed him to enter.
│
├── Important Exam Confusions
│   ├── Stop smoking = quit habit
│   ├── Stop to smoke = stop another work to smoke
│   ├── Remember locking = memory of past action
│   └── Remember to lock = future action reminder
│
└── Quick Difference
    ├── Gerund → Experience / Habit / After preposition
    ├── Infinitive → Purpose / Plan / Future
    └── Causative → Make others perform action

CONDITIONAL SENTENCES (IF-CLAUSES)
│
├── 1. TYPES OF CONDITIONALS
│   │
│   ├── (A) ZERO CONDITIONAL (Universal Truth)
│   │   ├── If + Present → Present
│   │   └── 👉 If you heat water, it boils
│   │
│   ├── (B) FIRST CONDITIONAL (Real Future)
│   │   ├── If + Present → will/shall + V1
│   │   └── 👉 If it rains, I will stay home
│   │
│   ├── (C) SECOND CONDITIONAL (Unreal / Imaginary)
│   │   ├── If + Past → would/could + V1
│   │   └── 👉 If I won the lottery, I would buy a car
│   │
│   ├── (D) THIRD CONDITIONAL (Past Unreal)
│   │   ├── If + Past Perfect → would/could + have + V3
│   │   └── 👉 If I had studied, I would have passed
│
├── 2. IMPORTANT RULE
│   ├── ❌ Never use "will" in IF-clause
│   └── ✔ Use Present instead
│
│   👉 ❌ If it will rain, I will go
│   👉 ✔ If it rains, I will go
│
├── 3. OTHER CONDITION WORDS
│   ├── unless = if not
│   │   👉 Unless you work hard, you will fail
│   │
│   ├── when, before, after
│   ├── as soon as
│   ├── until / till
│   ├── while
│   └── as long as
│
├── 4. SEQUENCE OF TENSE
│   │
│   ├── Past → Past
│   │   👉 He said he was tired
│   │
│   ├── Past → Present (Universal Truth)
│   │   👉 He said that the sun rises in the east
│   │
│   └── Present → Any tense
│       👉 He says he will come / came / comes
│
├── 5. TIME CLAUSES
│   │
│   ├── Rule:
│   │   ❌ No future in clause
│   │   ✔ Present in clause + Future in main
│   │
│   ├── Examples:
│   │   👉 I will call you when he comes
│   │   👉 I will eat after he arrives
│   │
│   ├── COMMON ERROR
│   │   ❌ When he will come, I will go
│   │   ✔ When he comes, I will go
│
├── 6. COMMON STRUCTURE
│   │
│   ├── If + Present → will + V1
│   ├── If + Past → would + V1
│   └── If + Past Perfect → would have + V3
│
└── 7. SSC EXAM FOCUS
    │
    ├── MOST ASKED
    │   ├── First Conditional
    │   ├── Third Conditional
    │   ├── Time Clause (when, after, before)
    │   └── unless
    │
    ├── COMMON ERROR TYPES
    │   ├── will in IF-clause ❌
    │   ├── wrong tense in time clause ❌
    │   ├── If I would… ❌
    │
    ├── IDENTIFICATION TRICK
    │   ├── Real → First
    │   ├── Imaginary → Second
    │   ├── Past regret → Third
    │
    └── 1-LINE RULE
        👉 If-clause NEVER takes future tense

VERBS USED IN SIMPLE PRESENT (NOT CONTINUOUS)
│
├── 1. RULE
│   └── Some verbs are NOT used in continuous tense
│       → Use Simple Present instead
│
├── 2. TYPES OF VERBS
│
│   ├── (A) Verbs of Perception
│   │   ├── see
│   │   ├── hear
│   │   ├── smell
│   │   ├── taste
│   │   └── feel
│
│   ├── (B) Verbs of Thinking / Knowledge
│   │   ├── think (opinion)
│   │   ├── know
│   │   ├── understand
│   │   ├── believe
│   │   └── remember
│
│   ├── (C) Possession Verbs
│   │   ├── have / has
│   │   ├── own
│   │   ├── possess
│   │   └── belong
│
│   ├── (D) Emotion / Feeling Verbs
│   │   ├── like
│   │   ├── love
│   │   ├── hate
│   │   ├── want
│   │   └── desire
│
│   └── (E) Other Verbs
│       ├── seem
│       ├── appear
│       └── imagine
│
├── 3. EXAMPLES
│
│   ├── ❌ My brother is owning a car.
│   └── ✅ My brother owns a car.
│
│   ├── ❌ I am knowing the answer.
│   └── ✅ I know the answer.
│
│   ├── ❌ She is liking ice cream.
│   └── ✅ She likes ice cream.
│
│   ├── ❌ I am understanding this topic.
│   └── ✅ I understand this topic.
│
│   ├── ❌ He is having a car.
│   └── ✅ He has a car.
│
├── 4. EXAM TRICK ⭐
│   ├── If verb shows:
│   │   → feeling
│   │   → possession
│   │   → knowledge
│   │
│   └── 👉 Use SIMPLE PRESENT (never continuous)
│
└── 5. EXCEPTION ⭐
    ├── Some verbs CAN be continuous with different meaning:
    │
    ├── have
    │   ├── I have a car (possession)
    │   └── I am having lunch (action) ✅
    │
    ├── think
    │   ├── I think he is right (opinion)
    │   └── I am thinking about it (process) ✅
    │
    └── see
        ├── I see the bird (perception)
        └── I am seeing a doctor (meeting) ✅

Malster
Meaning: Makes/deals in malt
Hindi: माल्ट बनाने/बेचने वाला

Malingerer
Meaning: Fakes illness to avoid duty
Hindi: बीमारी का बहाना करने वाला

Mud-slinger
Meaning: Damages others’ reputation by accusations
Hindi: बदनामी करने वाला

Diffident
Meaning: Lacking confidence; shy and hesitant Hindi: आत्मविश्वास की कमी वाला / संकोची

Important English Phrases & Usage
│
├── One by one
│   ├── Meaning → एक-एक करके
│   └── Example → The students entered the room one by one.
│
├── One after another
│   ├── Meaning → एक के बाद एक
│   └── Example → He won matches one after another.
│
├── Hotter and hotter
│   ├── Meaning → लगातार अधिक गर्म होना
│   └── Example → It is getting hotter and hotter.
│
├── Day by day
│   ├── Meaning → दिन-प्रतिदिन / धीरे-धीरे
│   └── Example → Day by day, it is getting hotter and hotter.
│
├── In time
│   ├── Meaning → समय से पहले / देर होने से पहले
│   └── Example → We reached the station in time to catch the train.
│
├── On time
│   ├── Meaning → ठीक समय पर
│   └── Example → The train arrived on time.
│
├── Important Difference
│   ├── In time → Before it is too late
│   └── On time → Exactly at scheduled time
│
└── Quick Trick
    └── In time = Before late | On time = Exact time

Non-Gradable / Absolute Adjectives
│
├── Definition
│   └── Adjectives that express complete or extreme qualities
│       and normally do not take comparative or superlative forms
│
├── Rule
│   └── Do not use more / most / -er / -est with them
│
├── Wrong vs Correct
│
│   ├── The glass is more empty now. ❌
│   │   └── The glass is empty now. ✔
│   │
│   ├── He is more chief than others. ❌
│   │   └── He is the chief. ✔
│   │
│   ├── This is more perfect. ❌
│   │   └── This is perfect. ✔
│   │
│   └── She is most unique. ❌
│       └── She is unique. ✔
│
├── Common Absolute Adjectives
│   ├── Chief
│   ├── Complete
│   ├── Perfect
│   ├── Unique
│   ├── Universal
│   ├── Absolute
│   ├── Empty
│   ├── Entire
│   ├── Dead
│   └── Impossible
│
├── Important Exception
│   ├── Beautiful → Gradable adjective
│   ├── Correct → More beautiful / Most beautiful
│   └── Not an absolute adjective
│
├── Examples
│   ├── This room is empty.
│   ├── She gave a perfect answer.
│   └── He is more beautiful than his brother.
│
└── Quick Trick
    └── Complete meaning already present → No comparison

Subject–Verb Agreement (Singular / Plural Rules)
│
├── ALL
│
│   ├── All + plural countable noun → Plural Verb
│   │   └── All the parties agree to support.
│   │
│   └── All + uncountable noun → Singular Verb
│       └── All the water is clean.
│
├── SOME OF
│
│   ├── Some of + uncountable noun → Singular Verb
│   │   └── Some of the water is dirty.
│   │
│   ├── Some of + plural noun/pronoun → Plural Verb
│   │   └── Some of them are coming.
│   │
│   └── Depends on noun after "of"
│
├── ONE OF
│
│   ├── One of + plural noun → Singular Verb
│   │   └── One of the students is absent.
│   │
│   └── One-third of + noun → Depends on noun
│       ├── One-third of the players are absent.
│       └── One-third of the cake is left.
│
├── NO OTHER
│
│   └── No other + singular noun + singular verb
│       └── No other student is as bright as her.
│
├── NUMBER RULES
│
│   ├── A number of + plural noun → Plural Verb
│   │   └── A number of students are absent.
│   │
│   └── The number of + plural noun → Singular Verb
│       └── The number of applicants is increasing.
│
├── MORE THAN ONE
│
│   ├── More than one + singular noun → Singular Verb
│   │   └── More than one student has passed.
│   │
│   └── More + plural noun + than one → Plural Verb
│       └── More teachers than one have joined.
│
├── ALWAYS SINGULAR
│
│   ├── Each / Every
│   ├── Everyone / Everybody
│   ├── Either / Neither
│   ├── One of + plural noun
│   ├── The number of + plural noun
│   ├── Uncountable nouns
│   ├── Subjects like News, Mathematics, Politics
│   ├── Time / Money / Distance as one unit
│   ├── Collective nouns (as one unit)
│   └── Two nouns referring to one thing
│
│   Examples:
│   ├── Mathematics is difficult.
│   ├── Ten rupees is enough.
│   ├── Bread and butter is my breakfast.
│   └── The team is winning.
│
├── ALWAYS PLURAL
│
│   ├── Both
│   ├── Many
│   ├── Few / Several
│   ├── A number of + plural noun
│   ├── Two subjects joined by "and"
│   └── Collective noun acting individually
│
│   Examples:
│   ├── Ram and Shyam are friends.
│   ├── Few students have passed.
│   └── The jury are arguing among themselves.
│
├── DEPENDS ON SUBJECT
│
